behavior: AC1: a stopped or unhealthy gateway fails the local health contract and the two-minute watcher emits one deduplicated incident through kubelab-notify@ after boot grace.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'healthcheck or notification_hooks or timer_interval'
evidence: Clean live stop at 21:22:43Z produced unhealthy, successful notifier and one ops-log incident at 21:22:47.606959Z; restart produced recovery after exactly 1 failed run at 21:23:44.059549Z.

behavior: AC2: healthy and one recent start (under 90s, RestartCount <= 1) succeed; sustained starting, repeated restart, unhealthy, missing and Docker errors fail; recovery ignores provider readiness.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'probe or recovery or simple_health'
evidence: 26 focused tests passed: healthy and one recent start <=90s with RestartCount <=1 succeed; sustained starting, repeated restart, stopped/unhealthy/missing/invalid state and Docker errors fail; invalid names exit 64 before Docker; recovery ignores provider readiness.

behavior: AC3: a powered-off ace2 cannot page because there is no external monitor, persistent timer or always-on dependency.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'on_demand or boot_grace or external_monitor'
evidence: Tests prove no Persistent/OnCalendar directive, Kuma monitor or egress dependency; ten-minute local boot grace and two-minute cadence are rendered. Power-off was not physically exercised; no external notification path exists.

behavior: AC4: disabling removes all watcher artifacts; enabling follows gateway health, and a failed deployment restores a paused timer before propagating the error.
